item: Row 370: the R801 restored-key marker's look-and-write is serialised across processes, not only threads
summary: A restore's look for an evidence key and its R801 marker write, and a new key's creation with its marker drop, ran under keyfile.KEY_FILES_LOCK alone (a lock inside one process), so a second server on the same data folder (R176) could make its own key between a restore's look and its marker and then read its own key as another installation's; both now run under evidence.restored_marker_lock, which takes a cross-process file_lock on keys.lock beside the keys folder (never inside it, so the folder holds only key files; app-owned for the erase by the .lock rule) FIRST and KEY_FILES_LOCK only once it is held, so nothing in this process waits on another process while holding the in-process lock and a stalled second server never holds up this process's key changes or emergency erase (both security reads' should-fix); re-entrant in a thread; the restore's end-of-run take-back is one step under it too; what the marker means is unchanged; a filesystem that cannot lock runs unlocked with file_lock's one warning, as before.
